shadow:
Listen for the word try in your own mouth. It shows up right when something is not moving on its own and you have decided to make it move anyway. You push. The thing pushes back. You push harder.

This is the oldest power there is. It cracked the first seeds open and shoved them up through the dirt. It does not think. It does not check whether the wall it is hitting is a real wall. It just keeps going, and a person under its grip cannot hear anyone telling them to stop, including their own body.

Most people read the resistance as a sign to lean in. Work harder, want it more. That is the misread. The resistance is information. It is the situation saying this is not the way through. The exhaustion at the end of a long stretch of forcing is not weakness. It is the part of you that was never fooled, finally loud enough to hear. The force is real and you will need it. It is just aimed wrong. Turn and listen to where the push is coming back at you, and it starts to show the easier road that was there the whole time.
repressive: Some people meet this power by hiding from it. They hand their say to other people, accept being walked over, call themselves small. The strength does not vanish. It backs up inside and turns into a tiredness with no obvious cause.
reactive: Others meet it by shoving outward. They bully, push their weight around, talk over the room, and turn furious the moment anyone names it. They cannot see they are doing it. The force is loud and the awareness has not caught up.
gift:
The turn is small. The same engine, pointed differently. Strength is force that has started listening, so it moves with the grain of a thing instead of against it.

Watch how an animal moves when it is not afraid. It does not strain. It is not really moving at all, it is being moved, and the difference is everything. Strength is effortless, and effortless does not mean easy. There can be enormous exertion. What is gone is the resistance that grinds. You feel it when you stop fighting the work and the work starts carrying you.

It comes from low down, from the belly and the base of the spine, not from the head where the trying lives. The head decides how things should go. The belly already knows how they want to go, without being able to explain itself. When you are rooted there, the answer arrives simple, because it did not come through thought at all. It came up through you.

This kind of strength cannot really be hidden. A person moving from their center carries a field around them that others feel before a word is said. The more they trust the easy line, the more the strength has somewhere to go.
siddhi:
There is a story of a drunk man raging on a train, and a young fighter rising to meet him, sure of his strength. Then an old man calls the drunk over and asks him about persimmon trees. By the next stop the raging man is weeping in the old man's lap. No force was used. Nothing was met head on.

That is majesty. It is past strength entirely. Strength still has an edge, still knows itself as strength against something. Majesty has no edge. It does not win. It reconciles, and it always finds the way that costs nothing.

Here the one who was doing the moving is simply gone. There is movement, and it is life moving, and the body has become a clear channel for it. This is where the old gestures came from, the dances and the forms, before anyone copied them. Pure life passing through a human shape with nothing added.

And the force at the very bottom, the blind primal push, was never the enemy. It was the same current. It just had not yet learned it was royal.
